claim: Histamine-dependent and -independent itch is conveyed by parallel peripheral neural pathways that express gastrin-releasing peptide (GRP) and neuromedin B (NMB), respectively, to the spinal cord of mice.
source: Histamine-dependent and -independent itch is conveyed by parallel peripheral neural pathways that express gastrin-releasing peptide (GRP) and neuromedin B (NMB), respectively, to the spinal cord of mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing these pathways.

claim: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) has been proposed to transmit both types of itch via its receptor NPRA encoded by Npr1.
source: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) has been proposed to transmit both types of itch via its receptor NPRA encoded by Npr1.
evidence: This claim references prior proposals in the literature about BNP-NPRA signaling in itch.

claim: BNP also binds to its cognate receptor, NPRC encoded by Npr3 with equal potency.
source: However, BNP also binds to its cognate receptor, NPRC encoded by Npr3 with equal potency.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about natriuretic peptide receptor binding affinities.

claim: Natriuretic peptides (NP) signal through the Gi-coupled inhibitory cGMP pathway that is supposed to inhibit neuronal activity.
source: Moreover, natriuretic peptides (NP) signal through the Gi-couped inhibitory cGMP pathway that is supposed to inhibit neuronal activity, raising the question of how BNP may transmit itch information.
evidence: This claim draws on established knowledge of natriuretic peptide signaling mechanisms.

claim: Npr3 expression in laminae I-II of the dorsal horn partially overlaps with NMB receptor (NMBR).
source: Here, we report that Npr3 expression in laminae I-II of the dorsal horn partially overlaps with NMB receptor (NMBR) that transmits histaminergic itch via Gq-couped PLCβ-Ca2+ signaling pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data presented in the manuscript showing overlapping expression patterns.

claim: NMBR transmits histaminergic itch via Gq-coupled PLCβ-Ca2+ signaling pathway.
source: Here, we report that Npr3 expression in laminae I-II of the dorsal horn partially overlaps with NMB receptor (NMBR) that transmits histaminergic itch via Gq-couped PLCβ-Ca2+ signaling pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by prior studies and data in the manuscript.

claim: NPRC is required for itch evoked by histamine but not chloroquine (CQ).
source: Functional studies indicate that NPRC is required for itch evoked by histamine but not chloroquine (CQ), a nonhistaminergic pruritogen.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data from siRNA knockdown experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: BNP significantly facilitates scratching behaviors mediated by NMB, but not GRP.
source: Importantly, BNP significantly facilitates scratching behaviors mediated by NMB, but not GRP.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral experiments showing BNP potentiation of NMB-induced scratching but not GRP-induced scratching.

claim: BNP evoked Ca2+ responses in NMBR/NPRC HEK 293 cells.
source: Consistently, BNP evoked Ca2+ responses in NMBR/NPRC HEK 293 cells and NMBR/NPRC dorsal horn neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from HEK 293 cells co-expressing NMBR and NPRC.

claim: BNP evoked Ca2+ responses in NMBR/NPRC dorsal horn neurons.
source: Consistently, BNP evoked Ca2+ responses in NMBR/NPRC HEK 293 cells and NMBR/NPRC dorsal horn neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data from cultured dorsal horn neurons.

claim: BNP facilitates NMB-encoded itch through a novel NPRC-NMBR cross-signaling in mice.
source: These results reveal a previously unknown mechanism by which BNP facilitates NMB-encoded itch through a novel NPRC-NMBR cross-signaling in mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple lines of evidence including behavioral, molecular, and calcium imaging data.

claim: GRP and NMB encode nonhistaminergic itch and histaminergic itch, respectively.
source: Notably, gastrin-releasing peptide (GRP) and neuromedin B (NMB), two mammalian neuropeptides, have been shown to encode nonhistaminergic itch and histaminergic itch, respectively (Akiyama et al., 2014; Barry et al., 2020; Sun and Chen, 2007; Wan et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Murine GRP-GRPR signaling is important for the development of contact dermatitis-induced itch.
source: Moreover, murine GRP-GRPR signaling is important for the development of contact dermatitis-induced itch (Chen et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2020; Shiratori-Hayashi et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Histaminergic and nonhistaminergic itch is transmitted through parallel primary afferent pathways.
source: These findings are in accordance with human and animal studies showing that histaminergic and nonhistaminergic itch is transmitted through parallel primary afferent pathways (Chen, 2021; Johanek et al., 2007; Namer et al., 2008; Roberson et al., 2013; Wilson et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to human and animal studies.

claim: BNP has been implicated in itch at discrete regions, including skin cells, sensory neurons, and spinal cord.
source: B-type or brain natriuretic peptide (BNP), encoded by the gene Nppb, has been implicated in itch at discrete regions, including skin cells, sensory neurons, and spinal cord (Liu et al., 2020; Meng et al., 2018; Mishra and Hoon, 2013; Solinski et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The natriuretic peptide (NP) family consists of atrial (ANP), B-type (BNP), and C-type natriuretic peptides (CNP).
source: The natriuretic peptide (NP) family also consists of atrial (ANP) and C-type natriuretic peptides (CNP) (Potter et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established knowledge about natriuretic peptides.

claim: BNP binds to both NPRA and NPRC with equal affinity, but not NPRB.
source: BNP binds to both NPRA and NPRC, encoded by Npr1 and Npr3, respectively, with equality affinity, but not NPRB, while ANP also binds NPRA directly, resulting in the elevation of the second message cyclic GMP concentration (Figure 1A; Potter et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: ANP binds NPRA directly, resulting in the elevation of cyclic GMP concentration.
source: BNP binds to both NPRA and NPRC, encoded by Npr1 and Npr3, respectively, with equality affinity, but not NPRB, while ANP also binds NPRA directly, resulting in the elevation of the second message cyclic GMP concentration (Figure 1A; Potter et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: NPRC is considered to function as a clearance or silent receptor.
source: Although NPRC is considered to function as a clearance or silent receptor (Maack et al., 1987), it can also mediate guanylyl cyclase (GC) receptor-coupled Gαisignaling under certain physiological conditions (Anand-Srivastava, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: NPRC can mediate guanylyl cyclase (GC) receptor-coupled Gαi signaling under certain physiological conditions.
source: Although NPRC is considered to function as a clearance or silent receptor (Maack et al., 1987), it can also mediate guanylyl cyclase (GC) receptor-coupled Gαisignaling under certain physiological conditions (Anand-Srivastava, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: BNP-NPRA signaling was initially proposed as an itch-specific pathway responsible for transmitting both histamine- and CQ-evoked itch that acts upstream of GRP-GRPR signaling.
source: BNP-NPRA signaling was initially proposed as an itch-specific pathway responsible for transmitting both histamine- and CQ-evoked itch that acts upstream of GRP-GRPR signaling (Huang et al., 2018; Mishra and Hoon, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior proposals.

claim: The proposal that BNP transmits all types of itch is at odds with the fact that GRP is required only for nonhistaminergic itch.
source: However, that BNP transmits all types of itch is at odds with the fact that GRP is required only for nonhistaminergic itch.
evidence: This claim is based on logical inference from established knowledge about GRP function.

claim: Genetic ablation of spinal Grp neurons fails to impact itch behaviors.
source: Further, genetic ablation of spinal Grp neurons fails to impact itch behaviors (Barry et al., 2020), indicating that spinal Grp neurons do not constitute a functional circuit for itch.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Spinal Grp neurons do not constitute a functional circuit for itch.
source: Further, genetic ablation of spinal Grp neurons fails to impact itch behaviors (Barry et al., 2020), indicating that spinal Grp neurons do not constitute a functional circuit for itch.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the cited finding that ablation of spinal Grp neurons does not affect itch.

claim: BNP-NPRA signaling is involved in histaminergic itch as well as chronic itch in mice which comprises the histaminergic component.
source: Recent studies have shown that BNP-NPRA signaling is involved in histaminergic itch as well as chronic itch in mice which comprises the histaminergic component (Liu et al., 2020; Solinski et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: The GC-cGMP signal transduction pathway mediated by BNP is inhibitory.
source: Considering that the GC-cGMP signal transduction pathway mediated by BNP is inhibitory (Potter et al., 2006) and that BNP-NPRA/NPRC signaling may exert an inhibitory rather than excitatory function, analogous to GαI protein-coupled signaling, it is paradoxical that BNP would transmit rather than inhibiting itch information.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established knowledge about BNP signaling.

claim: BNP dose-dependently evoked scratching behaviors 60 min after i.t. injection.
source: (B) BNP dose-dependently evoked scratching behaviors 60 min after i.t. injection. n = 6. *p < 0.05, **p < 0.01, one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's test.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: BNP-induced scratching behavior shows a delayed onset of scratching responses.
source: (C) Time-course of scratching behaviors induced by different doses of BNP shows a delayed onset of scratching responses.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-course data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Npr1 and Grpr show minimal overlapping expression in laminae I-II of the dorsal horn.
source: (D, F, H, J, L, N) Images of double RNAscope ISH showing that the overlapping expression of Npr1 (green) with Grpr (red) (D), Nmbr (F), of Npr3 (green) with Nmbr (red) (H), Npr3 (red) with Vglut2 (green) (J), Vgat (green) (L), or Npr1 (green) (N) in laminae I-II of the dorsal horn.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 1D and quantified in Figure 1E.

claim: Approximately 47.8% of Npr3+ neurons express Nmbr.
source: By contrast, approximately 47.8% of Npr3+ + express Nmbr (Figure 1H,I), raising the possibility that NPRC is involved in crosstalk with NMBR.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 1H and quantified in Figure 1I.

claim: 64.6% of Npr3+ neurons are excitatory neurons and 32.0% are inhibitory neurons.
source: Remarkably, Npr3+ + are predominantly restricted to lamina I-II (Figure 1H, J, L, N, 5C) with 64.6% being excitatory neurons and 32.0% being inhibitory neurons (Figure 1J–M).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data showing co-expression with Vglut2 and Vgat markers.

claim: ANP at doses of 1-20 µg (equivalent to 6-120 µM, i.t.) failed to induce robust scratching behaviors in mice.
source: (A) ANP 1 ~ 20 µg, (equivalent to 6–120 µM, i.t.) failed to induce robust scratching behaviors in mice. n = 6.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Only BNP (30 µM, i.t.) facilitated histamine itch, whereas neither ANP (60 µM, i.t.) nor CNP (60 µM, i.t.) exhibited facilitatory effect.
source: (B) Only BNP (30 µM, i.t.) facilitated histamine itch. Note that neither ANP (60 µM, i.t.) nor CNP (60 µM, i.t.) exhibited facilitatory effect. n = 6–7. *p < 0.05, ***p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett's test.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Innervations of peptidergic CGRP+ and non-peptidergic IB4+ primary afferents in the superficial dorsal horn of Npr1 KO mice are comparable with wild-type littermates.
source: We found that innervations of peptidergic CGRP+ and non-peptidergic IB4+ primary afferents in the superficial dorsal horn of Npr1 KO mice are comparable with wild-type (WT) littermates (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The innervations of TRPV1+, GRP+, and SP+ primary afferents are comparable between WT and Npr1 KO mice.
source: The innervations of TRPV1+, GRP+, and SP+ primary afferents are also comparable between WT and Npr1 KO mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B-D), indicating that NPRA is dispensable for the innervation of primary afferents.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B-D.

claim: NPRA is dispensable for the innervation of primary afferents.
source: The innervations of TRPV1+, GRP+, and SP+ primary afferents are also comparable between WT and Npr1 KO mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B-D), indicating that NPRA is dispensable for the innervation of primary afferents.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that primary afferent innervation is normal in Npr1 KO mice.

source: (G) Scratching behaviors elicited by i.t. BNP (150 µM) were significantly enhanced by isoflurane.

evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: Npr2 siRNA had no effect on CQ and histamine itch.
source: Npr2 siRNA had no effect on CQ and histamine itch, making it unlikely to be involved in itch transmission (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 2C and 2D.

claim: BNP-sap at 2.5 µg reduced the number of Npr1+ neurons to approximately 50%.
source: RNAscope ISH showed that the number of Npr1+ + were reduced to ~50% (82.9 ± 3.3 in control vs. 39.8 ± 2.2 in BNP-sap) (Figure 5A,F), whereas Npr2+ neurons were not affected (288.0 ± 18.2 in control vs. 300.5 ± 7.8 in BNP-sap) (Figure 5B and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 5A and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: BNP-sap did not affect Npr2+ neurons.
source: RNAscope ISH showed that the number of Npr1+ + were reduced to ~50% (82.9 ± 3.3 in control vs. 39.8 ± 2.2 in BNP-sap) (Figure 5A,F), whereas Npr2+ neurons were not affected (288.0 ± 18.2 in control vs. 300.5 ± 7.8 in BNP-sap) (Figure 5B and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 5B and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: BNP-sap ablated approximately 67% of Npr3+ neurons.
source: Moreover, BNP-sap ablated ~67% of Npr3+ neurons (41.8 ± 1.4 in control vs. 13.8 ± 1.8 in BNP-sap) as well as ~37% of Grp+ + (44.6 ± 1.9 in control vs. 22.6 ± 2.0 in BNP-sap) (Figure 5C, D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 5C and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: BNP-sap ablated approximately 37% of Grp+ neurons.
source: Moreover, BNP-sap ablated ~67% of Npr3+ neurons (41.8 ± 1.4 in control vs. 13.8 ± 1.8 in BNP-sap) as well as ~37% of Grp+ + (44.6 ± 1.9 in control vs. 22.6 ± 2.0 in BNP-sap) (Figure 5C, D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 5D and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: The number of Nmbr+ neurons was significantly reduced after BNP-sap injection.
source: As expected, the number of Nmbr+ neurons was also significantly reduced after BNP-sap injection, likely due to Npr3 expression in these neurons (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope ISH data shown in Figure 5E and quantified in Figure 5F.

claim: BNP internalized NPRA and NPRC, but not NPRB, in HEK 293 cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by internalization assay data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: BNP-sap could ablate both NPRA and NPRC cells.
source: Indeed, BNP internalized NPRA and NPRC, but not NPRB, in HEK 293 cells (Figure 5G), indicating that BNP-sap could ablate both NPRA and NPRC cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that BNP internalizes both NPRA and NPRC receptors.

claim: Histamine itch was significantly reduced in BNP-sap mice.

claim: CQ itch was not affected in BNP-sap mice.
source: Interestingly, behavioral studies showed that histamine itch was significantly reduced in BNP-sap mice (Figure 5H), whereas CQ itch was not affected (Figure 5I).

claim: NPRA and NPRC neurons in the spinal cord play an important role in histamine itch.

evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that BNP-sap treatment reduces histamine itch.

claim: The levels of Nppb mRNA in dry-skin mice were significantly reduced.

claim: I.t. SST-evoked scratching was markedly reduced but not abolished by intraperitoneal injection (i.p.) of morphine.
source: I.t. SST-evoked scratching was markedly reduced but not abolished by intraperitoneal injection (i.p.) of morphine (Figure 6A), a method used to evaluate whether i.t. induced scratching/biting behavior reflects pain (Hylden and Wilcox, 1981).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Scratching behaviors evoked by i.t. injection of SST were significantly attenuated in mice with bombesin-saporin (BB-sap) treatment.
source: In addition, scratching behaviors evoked by i.t. injection of SST and octreotide (OCT), a selective SST2R agonist, were significantly attenuated on mice with bombesin-saporin (BB-sap) treatment, which can completely block nonhistaminergic itch transmission (Sun et al., 2009; Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Scratching behaviors evoked by i.t. injection of octreotide (OCT) were significantly attenuated in mice with bombesin-saporin (BB-sap) treatment.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of SST2R neurons could result in disinhibition of both itch and pain transmission.

claim: Stimulation at all frequencies failed to evoke significant scratching behaviors in Sst-ChR2 mice compared to Sst-cre mice.

evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: BNP can function as a neuromodulator, rather than a neurotransmitter, to facilitate itch transmission.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that in sensory neurons, BNP can function as a neuromodulator, rather than a neurotransmitter, to facilitate itch transmission.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple lines of evidence including behavioral and calcium imaging data.

claim: NPRC in the spinal cord is crucial for mediating BNP-facilitated histaminergic itch.
source: We also show that NPRC in the spinal cord is crucial for mediating BNP-facilitated histaminergic itch.
evidence: This claim is supported by siRNA knockdown and pharmacological experiments.

claim: BNP alone could not activate Ca2+ transients either in HEK293 cells or in the dorsal horn neurons.
source: By demonstrating that BNP alone could not activate Ca2+ transients either in HEK293 cells or in the dorsal horn neurons, we verify that BNP is an inhibitory neuropeptide, in line with the observation that i.t. BNP, even at very high doses (2.5–5 µg), fails to induce the rapid onset of scratching behavior, typical for ligand-mediated acute activation of excitatory itch receptors in the spinal cord (Sun and Chen, 2007; Wan et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data.

claim: BNP is an inhibitory neuropeptide.
source: By demonstrating that BNP alone could not activate Ca2+ transients either in HEK293 cells or in the dorsal horn neurons, we verify that BNP is an inhibitory neuropeptide, in line with the observation that i.t. BNP, even at very high doses (2.5–5 µg), fails to induce the rapid onset of scratching behavior, typical for ligand-mediated acute activation of excitatory itch receptors in the spinal cord (Sun and Chen, 2007; Wan et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is inferred from calcium imaging and behavioral data.

claim: BNP becomes excitatory by facilitating NMB-mediated itch transmission.
source: However, BNP becomes excitatory by facilitating NMB-mediated itch transmission.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral and calcium imaging data showing BNP potentiation of NMB signaling.

claim: Distinct modes of action for neuropeptides coordinate itch transmission in the spinal cord.
source: Thus. distinct modes of action for neuropeptides coordinate itch transmission in the spinal cord.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the findings that different neuropeptides have different roles in itch transmission.

claim: BNP and SST are not involved in the development of dry skin and neuropathic itch in mice.
source: Thus, BNP and SST are not involved in the development of dry skin and neuropathic itch in mice.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observations that Npr1 KO mice show normal dry skin itch and Nppb/Sst are downregulated in chronic itch models.

claim: Inhibitory GI-coupled receptors enhance or facilitate the activation of the canonical PLCβ−Ca2+ signaling transduction pathway downstream of Gq-coupled receptors.
source: Numerous studies have shown that inhibitory GI-coupled receptors enhance or facilitate the activation of the canonical PLCβ−Ca2+ signaling transduction pathway downstream of Gq-coupled receptors (Prezeau et al., 2010; Werry et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: NPRC-NMBR represents the first example of the crosstalk between a non-GPCR inhibitory receptor and an excitatory GPCR.
source: Nevertheless, NPRC-NMBR represents the first example of the crosstalk between a non-GPCR inhibitory receptor and an excitatory GPCR.
evidence: This claim is based on the novel finding of NPRC-NMBR crosstalk and knowledge that NPRC is not a typical GPCR.

claim: Cutaneous activation of Nppb/Sst fibers failed to evoke scratching behavior.
source: The finding that cutaneous activation of BNP/SST fibers failed to evoke scratching behavior suggests that activation of these fibers does not transmit itch information as a functional entity.
evidence: This claim is supported by optogenetic stimulation data.

claim: Activation of BNP/SST fibers does not transmit itch information as a functional entity.

claim: DRG-specific deletion of Sst did not influence itch transmission.
source: However, they are consistent with the observation that DRG-specific deletion of Sst did not influence itch transmission (Huang et al., 2018).

claim: The role of SST in sensory neurons is limited to the disinhibition of certain types of pain by inhibiting SST2R inhibitory neurons gating nociceptive transmission.
source: Thus, the role of SST in sensory neurons is limited to the disinhibition of certain types of pain by inhibiting SST2R inhibitory neurons gating nociceptive transmission (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including behavioral and molecular data.

claim: Current mouse models of chronic itch, including allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) and atopic dermatitis (AD), are additionally mediated by histamine-dependent mechanisms.
source: However, current mouse models of chronic itch, including allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) and atopic dermatitis (AD), are additionally mediated by histamine-dependent mechanisms, as they are chemically induced allergic inflammatory responses that involve histamine release from mast cells (Shim and Oh, 2008; Wang and Kim, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In ACD and AD mouse models, BNP may be upregulated in DRGs as a result of mast cell degranulation and may facilitate histaminergic itch.

evidence: This claim is based on inference from prior studies and the findings of the current study.

claim: BNP potently enhances NMB function, but not vice versa.
source: Considering that BNP potently enhances NMB function, but not vice versa, these studies suggest that neuropeptides in sensory neurons either encode or modulate itch information (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral data showing BNP facilitates NMB but NMB does not facilitate histamine itch.
